absent: Consumer addition path, probe allocation, tree insertion and removal, and reference counting lifecycle outside routed range.
Low level breakpoint insertion and original instruction restoration mechanics and reference counter update implementation.
Architecture instruction analysis acceptance rules, trap and single-step handling, and valid mapping predicates.
Handler and return handler dispatch chains, uretprobe timer reclamation, and hybrid probe state transitions.
Stable address space checks, duplication semaphore implementation, and interruptible lock failure semantics.

findings.text: Registration creates a probe for a given inode offset pair after validating caller supplied consumer and file capabilities. It requires at least one callback, readable backing or shared anonymous support, offset within file size, and alignment of probe and reference counter offsets. On success it links the consumer and propagates breakpoints to existing mappings; on propagation failure it detaches the consumer, waits for grace periods, and reports failure.

Unregistration without synchronization detaches a consumer under exclusive registration control, revisits current mappings to withdraw breakpoints where no consumer remains, warns and retains the probe object on error, otherwise releases a reference. The companion synchronization operation waits for trace and return probe grace periods so that handler iteration can no longer enter removed consumer callbacks.

Application re-evaluates an already linked consumer across current mappings, installing or withdrawing breakpoints according to a boolean direction flag. It searches the consumer list under trace protection while holding exclusive registration control and reports absence when the supplied consumer is not linked.

Architecture overridable defaults supply out of line placement hints near the top of user address space, a default return trampoline encoding with its length, and a copy routine that initializes a slot and flushes data cache without user cache maintenance.

Mapping hooks integrate probes with address space lifetime. Creation of a writable private mapping with probe state first advances delayed reference counters, then installs matching probes from the global tree unless a fatal signal is pending. Unmapping only marks recalculation when the affected range overlaps a probe and the process is not exiting. Fork duplication propagates probe presence and forces recalculation in the child, while teardown releases delayed entries and out of line resources.

Instruction capture reads original bytes from page cache through either filesystem folio support or shared memory paging, bounded by file size and page remainder, accumulating until the architecture buffer is filled. Preparation runs at most once per probe under exclusive consumer control, rejecting breakpoint-like encodings and architecture analysis failures before publishing readiness with ordering against the trap handler.

Consumer selection treats a missing predicate as acceptance and otherwise defers to the consumer supplied test for a given address space. Chain evaluation scans the consumer list under shared consumer control and succeeds when any member accepts, otherwise reports no interest.

Installation ensures one-time preparation, optimistically records probe presence before attempting low level breakpoint insertion, confirms recalculation state on success, and reverts the optimistic mark when the first insertion fails. Withdrawal unconditionally requests later recalculation and then restores the original instruction through the low level helper.

Probe discovery orders entries by inode identity then file offset. Range search descends the ordered tree to any node inside the interval, list construction expands to predecessors and successors while the inode matches and offsets remain inside bounds, acquiring references on entries that are still alive, and unmapping checks use the same range test to decide recalculation.

Out of line support provides one reserved page per address space through a non-copyable sealed executable special mapping that refuses relocation and resolves faults to a shared page. Area creation reserves the initial slot for the return trampoline supplied by architecture code and publishes the area with release ordering. Slot management scans a bitmap for a free index with atomic claim, blocks on a wait queue until one appears, copies the out of line variant, and on release clears the bit with ordering and wakes waiters when present.

Breakpoint and trap address derivation prefers recorded task state when a probe is active on the current task and otherwise derives the location from the current instruction pointer adjusted for breakpoint instruction length. A weak default supplies the pointer based computation for architectures without overrides.

Return probe bookkeeping reuses instance objects through a per-task pool. Insertion resets consumption state and links to the head, removal unlinks the head when present, and final release either recycles immediately when the per-task sequence counter shows no concurrent timer scan or defers destruction through delayed reclamation when a scan may be active, optionally consuming and finalizing associated hybrid probe state first.

Withdrawal from a single address space iterates all mappings under exclusive control, skipping invalid or non-matching files and offsets outside the mapping extent before withdrawing. Delayed reference processing scans a global list under mutex, updating counters only for entries matching the faulting address space with a valid reference mapping, accumulating first error while continuing.

Collection of affected address spaces uses a singly linked node carrying a successor link, a referenced address space pointer, and the virtual address corresponding to the probe file offset. Helper releases a node and returns its successor for iterative cleanup.

Consumer membership and one-time preparation are serialized by a per-probe read write semaphore, exclusive for mutation and preparation, shared for chain scans. Registration and bulk mapping walks are serialized by a per-probe registration semaphore held exclusively. Global probe tree range searches use a dedicated lock in shared mode, while per-inode mapping mutexes serialize probe list construction during mapping changes and a global mutex guards delayed reference work.

Bulk installation across existing mappings coordinates with concurrent fork and address space mutation. The walker holds the duplication semaphore exclusively and acquires each target address space exclusively, validating stable address space state and mapping identity before acting. Fork helpers acquire the same duplication semaphore in shared mode, and out of line area insertion uses an interruptible exclusive address space acquisition with duplicate detection.

Bulk propagation proceeds through collection, validation, and action phases. Collection first attempts lightweight allocation under read side reverse mapping control and on shortage releases references, preallocates sufficient nodes, and retries. The action loop then validates each mapping and either installs when registering and the new consumer accepts, or withdraws when unregistering and the remaining chain rejects, releasing references and nodes as it advances.

Partial success and concurrency hazards are handled conservatively. Failed registration may have invoked the new consumer already and therefore synchronizes after detachment. Mapping installation tolerates concurrent unregistration because an emptied chain naturally skips work. Reverse mapping collection avoids reclaim recursion through non-blocking allocation with retry. Duplicate area insertion is reported as already present, and slot release warns once when the computed offset lies outside the reserved page.
Probe file offset alignment equals breakpoint instruction size and reference counter offset alignment equals short integer width; misaligned registration requests are rejected.
Out of line area occupies a single page with slot zero reserved for trampoline use and remaining capacity determined by a slots-per-page constant and per-slot byte size.
